I'm reworking the loop so it only returns when it finds an untrusted IP scanning right-to-left, falling back to the leftmost entry if everything's trusted — but I should verify this matches the existing test expectations for validateHeader.

Checking the "only trust RemoteAddr" test case: with trustedProxies set to just 40.40.40.40 and remoteIP trusted, walking the XFF header in reverse finds 30.30.30.30 untrusted first, so that becomes the client IP — confirming the logic returns the first untrusted address encountered.

But for the "all steps trusted" case, expecting 20.20.20.20, the current code returns as soon as it hits any trusted IP or i==0, which would incorrectly return 30.30.30.30 at i=1 since it's trusted. That's the bug — the code should continue past trusted IPs (unless i==0) and only return early when it finds an untrusted one, or reach the start of the list.

I'm rewriting the loop condition so that reaching i==0 always returns, but trusted IPs at other indices cause the loop to continue rather than exit early.

Checking the reported bug scenario against the trace: with proxies=[30.30.30.30], the loop skips the trusted hop and returns the leftmost entry once i==0, confirming this fix behaves correctly.

data.content:
All tests pass.

Fix: in `gin.go`'s `validateHeader`, the X-Forwarded-For scan was returning the current entry whenever it *was* a trusted proxy, instead of continuing past it; changed the condition to return only when the entry is untrusted (or leftmost), so trusted proxy hops are skipped and the real client IP (20.20.20.20) is returned.
